A Salve for sundry sores called
the Leaden plaister
XXVII

Take one pt of oyle olive of the best 1/2 a pounde
lead very well cerused wth dust 12 ounces of
Spanish soape incorporate all these well together in
an earthen pot well placed & when the lead is incor=
porated that the soape appeares & put it upon
a small fire of coales continuancye put oyle vntill six
houres & a halfe still stirring it on a bolt of [byres?]
fastened to a sticke of wood, yt make yt fire some
what bigger till the reddish be turned into a grey
colour but yt must not leave stirrings till the
matter be turned into the coulour of oyle some=
darker, then drop it on a wooden trencher or a
marble close to yt fingers nor the trencher [fashioneth?]
enoughe then dippy theades in that, the chardse or
thereone dipped will last 20 yeares, p of glovs yt brase
this plaister laid to the stomach Comforts appetite and
takes away the paines of the Stomack laid to the
[naile?] tis a remedy for the Celendine laid to the
reines of the back it stops the bloody fluxe

Openings of the reines bloat of the Kidney or workethe
of the back, it heales all swellings, Aches & bruises, as
frankes fistuloes, Imposthumes, pustes & felons them in
bringes applyed to the fundament it heales all diseases
thereon laid to the head, it is good for the wrinckles

A Tried Cordiall for Mris Nowell in Childbed
XXVIII

Take a quarter of a pint of Cowslip water & ounces of
Syrup of Clary & Gilliflowers & a pennyworth of Cinnamon
water & a Spoonfulls of Claron wine & Mounns
drams mingle all these together and it is a soveraigne
[...] cordiall for any especially for one that lyes
in Childbed

Pills for the Gall
XXIX

Take one handfull of Sallandine & as much bay
salt as can take up & twixte yt finger & Thumbe &
the iuice of halfe a Lemon stamp yt together in a
Mortar & straine the iuice out & small this place of
it put some of the hearbs upon it, vse this goe a
togither dressing it 3 or 4 times in a Day
together &c

A Salve for sundry vses called
the Leaden plaister
XXVII

Take one pound of oyle olive of the best 1 pound of white
Lead very well calcinated into dust, 12 ounces of
Spanish sope incorporate all these well together in
an earthen pott well glazed & when they be well incor=
porated that the sope comes upermost & put it upon
a small fire of coales, continueinge the said fire an
houre & a halfe still stirring it with a bolt of Iron
fastned to a Stick of wood, then make your fire some
what bigger, till the redness be turned into a grey
collour but you must not leave stirringe till the
matter be turned into the colour of oyle somewhat
darker, then drop it on a wooden trenchar & if it
neither cleave to your fingers nor the trenchar t'is boyled
enough, then dipp your cloathes in that, the Searclothes
therein dipped will last 20 yeares, & the older the better
this plaister laid to the stomach provokes appetite and
takes away the paine of the Stomach layd to the
belly, t'is a remedy for the Collicke laid to the
reines of the back it stops the bloudy flux

XXVIII

Syrrup of Clovegillyflowers & 2 pennyworth of Cinamon
water & 2 Spoonefulls of Clarett wine & Alcemus one
dramme mingle all these together and it is a soverai=
gne cordiall for any especially for one that lyes
in Childbed

XXIX
